correctness.rationale: The claim concerns sentences of rank at most three over nonempty finite structures in the pure equivalence language. Capping each block at size three and the number of blocks of each capped size at three is a two-sided game strategy: at most two blocks or points can have been used before any move requiring a fresh one. For an independent finite check, a rooted type can be encoded by the size of the root's block capped at three, and the set of pairs (other block contains at least two points, there is a third block) taken over other blocks. The absence of other blocks gives the empty set. If the second choice repeats the root or is in its own block, the capped size and existence of another block determine all last moves; if in another block, a fresh last point can be in either selected block or a third, exactly as recorded. These features are recoverable from the extension types. Grouping the 63 capped vectors by the sets of these rooted types reproduced 16 pair types, 18 rooted types, 21 sentence theories, all 21 listed unique minima and their size sum 103. The 12 atomic triple types also follow by enumerating the equivalence partitions of three slots and their equality refinements. Any nontrivial capping strictly reduces order, so a global minimum must itself be a capped vector. The rank-three conjunction requiring three blocks and at least three points in every block gives the sharp lower bound nine, and the finite extension-type characteristic sentences give all 2^21 unions of theories.
residual_risks: The replay is finite; the symbolic game reduction is required for the unrestricted finite family. No formal verification or external attestation is claimed.
